title: Objective Translation Workbench and Guardrail Spec
creator: Asha Khandelwal
description:
Goal: Create an operational workbench and accompanying guardrails that systematically translate company-level OKRs into clear, prioritized initiatives with explicit owners, stage gates, and escalation paths across Product, Eng, Design, and GTM.

Why: Current handoffs from company OKRs -> initiatives -> squads are ad hoc. This causes misaligned scope, duplicate work, unclear decision rights, and brittle dependencies during quarterly execution. The workbench will reduce friction for intake, make trade-offs explicit, and enable automated monitoring of commitment health.

Scope:
- Definition: canonical mapping template (Objective -> Outcome metrics -> Initiative -> Deliverables -> Squad owner -> Dependencies)
- Guardrails: required rubric for prioritization (impact, effort, uncertainty), capacity hedges, and rollback criteria
- Stage gates: Intake -> Scoping -> Ready-for-Commit -> Execution -> Rollout -> Closeout, with artifact checklist at each gate
- Decision rights matrix: who can re-scope, escalate, reallocate capacity, and sign off on rollouts
- Operational artifacts: Confluence templates, Linear automation (labels, required fields), and a lightweight dashboard to track initiative health vs OKR metrics

Non-goals: building a full PM tool or replacing existing OKR trackers; this is a pragmatic playbook and a set of minimal automations to improve alignment.

Acceptance criteria:
1) A published Workbench template in Confluence with examples for 2 company-level OKRs
2) Linear Intake form + required metadata enforced for new initiatives (key fields validated)
